newsitem.title: SPAIN: PM says Spain will obey court on dirty war papers.
newsitem.headline: PM says Spain will obey court on dirty war papers.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, in an interview published on Sunday, said his government would obey any Supreme Court order to declassify secret papers on a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatists.

"If the Supreme Court issues a verdict or an order, the government is obliged to follow it, as is natural," Aznar told Catalan daily La Vanguardia. "Nobody would suggest that the government declare itself in contempt of the Supreme Court."
The court on Friday admitted part of an appeal against the conservative government's decision in August to keep the military intelligence documents under lock and key for reasons of state security.

The appeal, if successful, would allow judges to deepen their investigation into allegations that officials in the previous Socialist administration oversaw a death squad campaign against Basque rebels which killed 27 people between 1983 and 1987.

The Socialists' first interior minister Jose Barrionuevo has been charged with creating and funding the self-styled GAL (Anti-terrorist Liberation Groups) that waged the illegal campaign against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Aznar was keen to distance his party from any wrong-doing.

"This government does not have the slightest responsibility in the GAL affair, nor any other event linked to it," Aznar told La Vanguardia. "I want the justice system to clear this up as soon as possible."
Former Socialist prime minister Felipe Gonzalez last week denied any state terrorism took place during his 13-year rule.
